name: Mediterranean Baked White Fish with Tomatoes, Olives and Bulgur

components.name: Baked Fish with Tomato & Olives

ingredients.name: Olive oil for fish and topping

steps: Heat oven to 220 C. Pat fish dry, season both sides, and arrange in a lightly oiled baking dish.
Toss tomatoes, olives, onion, garlic and herbs with oil and lemon, then scatter the mixture around and over the fish.
Bake 15-20 minutes, depending on thickness, until centre of fish reaches 63 C and vegetables release their juices.
Portion bulgur separately from fish and tomato mixture so juices do not make the grains soggy before serving.

components.name: Bulgur Wheat
steps: Cook dry bulgur in measured water according to its grade, then cover off heat until tender and steam has absorbed.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
Measured bulgur side is new; the source fish dish is lower-calorie without a grain.
Planning: SECONDARY STOVETOP: bulgur needs boiling.
Freezer: fish less attractive after freezing; cooked grains freeze well
Dietary: Contains fish, wheat; olives are high in salt.

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder, for 3–4 days at most, and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish and shellfish to 63°C and reheat leftovers to at least 74°C.

flags.shelfLife: Fish — plan for days 1-3; bulgur freezes well.
